name: Chaser
metaDescription: Chaser automates receivables for companies from £199 a month. docstoc drafts chase emails for $14.99 a month and you send them. Compare both.
headline: A Chaser alternative for people who write their own chasers
sub: Chaser runs receivables for finance teams; docstoc only drafts the email, so it costs far less and you keep the send button.
whatItIs: Chaser is accounts receivable automation and cash flow forecasting software. It chases invoices by email, SMS and automated calls, offers a customer payment portal, credit reports and late payment fees, and syncs with Xero, QuickBooks Online, Sage, NetSuite and others. It also offers debt collection services and a managed credit control service. Plans are tiered by company revenue, which suits finance teams with hundreds of open invoices.
whereTheyAreStronger: Chasing beyond email: SMS, automated phone calls and letters, with call recording on higher plans.
Two-way sync with accounting systems such as Sage, NetSuite, SAP and Dynamics 365 Business Central, not only Xero and QuickBooks.
A payment portal and Chaser Pay, so customers can pay from the reminder.
Credit monitoring, cash flow forecasting and optional human credit control through Chaser Care.
whereDocstocFits: You chase a few dozen invoices and mainly need the wording right for the number of days overdue.
You want to read every email before it goes out. docstoc never sends for you.
You would rather pay a flat $14.99 a month than choose a plan by company revenue.
You also need document templates or a certificate for a file, which come with the same account.

comparison.competitor: At the time of writing, receivables plans start at £199 a month (Compact, $259 in USD), with Core at £599 and Complete at £899. Annual billing takes 10% off.
comparison.docstoc: Pro is $14.99 a month. Business is $39.99 a month. The free tier gives 5 drafts a month without signing up.

comparison.competitor: Sends reminders by email, SMS and automated calls on schedules you set.
comparison.docstoc: Writes the draft. You copy it into Gmail, Outlook or Apple Mail and send it yourself.

comparison.competitor: Xero, QuickBooks Online, Sage, NetSuite, SAP, Dynamics 365 Business Central, plus API and CSV.
comparison.docstoc: QuickBooks Online and Xero on Pro, plus CSV upload and manual paste.

comparison.competitor: Credit reports, debtor risk insights, payment plans and a debt collection service.
comparison.docstoc: No credit checks and no collection service. Business adds a client payment risk score and a formal demand letter draft.

comparison.competitor: Companies with a finance function and revenue to match the plan tiers.
comparison.docstoc: Freelancers and small businesses that chase by hand today.

whenToChoose.competitor: Choose Chaser if several people handle receivables, you want automated calls and SMS, need a payment portal, or want credit reports and a team to take over collections. Its sync with larger accounting systems matters at that size.
whenToChoose.docstoc: Choose docstoc if you send your own reminders and want help with tone and timing. It is a drafting tool, not an automated sender, and it does not replace credit control or debt collection.

faq.q: Is docstoc cheaper than Chaser?
faq.a: Yes, on published prices at the time of writing. Chaser's Compact plan is £199 a month; docstoc Pro is $14.99 a month. They do different jobs: Chaser automates the whole chase, docstoc drafts the email.

faq.q: Can docstoc send reminders automatically like Chaser?
faq.a: No. docstoc writes the email and you send it from your own mailbox. That is deliberate, so no client hears from you without your say.

faq.q: Can I move my open invoices from Chaser?
faq.a: Yes. Export unpaid invoices as CSV or connect QuickBooks or Xero on Pro, then generate drafts. Turn off Chaser's automated sending first so clients do not get two reminders.

sources.supports: Plan prices (Compact £199/$259, Core £599, Complete £899), 10% annual discount, revenue tiers, SMS/call credits, call recording, Chaser Care, collection service
Features: email/SMS/auto-call chasing, portal, Chaser Pay, credit reports, forecasting, integrations list
docstoc facts: Pro $14.99, Business $39.99, 5 free drafts a month, draft-only, QuickBooks/Xero on Pro, templates, boundaries

existingClaimIssues: 'Compact from ~$259/mo' is correct for monthly USD billing at the time checked; GBP prices exclude VAT and annual billing is 10% cheaper, so say 'from £199 a month'.
'No per-seat / revenue ladder' is a docstoc claim; Chaser's current plans are revenue tiers (legacy invoice-based plans also exist). Wording should say that the tiers are by revenue, not seat count.
Page uses em dashes as connectors, against the style guide.
gaps: Chaser's own help page says pricing moved; I used the detailed pricing page. Did not verify whether SOC 2 claim on chaserhq.com is current, so left it out.

name: Paidnice
metaDescription: Paidnice runs scheduled reminders for Xero and QuickBooks from $69 a month. docstoc drafts chase emails for $14.99 and you send them.

whatItIs: Paidnice is accounts receivable automation for Xero and QuickBooks. It applies your payment terms to your invoices and chases them before, on and after the due date. It also emails statements, adds late fees your terms allow, reads customer replies, offers a payment portal and escalates overdue accounts to a person. Its own page says nothing runs until you approve the policies.
whereTheyAreStronger: Reminders, statements and late fees run on a schedule from your ledger, so the work happens without you.
Customer replies are read and logged, with promises and questions noted and next steps drafted.
A payment portal with card, bank transfer and payment plans.
Usage-based tiers by invoice volume, with multi-currency, webhooks and an API on Pro.
whereDocstocFits: You want to see and edit each email before it leaves your inbox.
You send a handful of reminders a month, where a $69 plan is more than the job needs.
You are not on Xero or QuickBooks and prefer CSV or pasting an invoice.
You want free templates for payment reminders and contracts next to the drafts.

comparison.competitor: At the time of writing: Essentials $69 a month for up to 150 invoices, Pro from $99 a month by invoice volume, Custom from $999. First 20 actions free.
comparison.docstoc: Pro $14.99 a month, Business $39.99 a month. 5 free drafts a month with no signup.

comparison.competitor: Scheduled reminders, statements and fees once you approve the policies, with some items set to wait for approval.
comparison.docstoc: No scheduled sending. Each draft is generated on request and you send it.

comparison.competitor: Adds fees or interest your terms allow, posts them to your ledger and tells the customer.
comparison.docstoc: No fee engine and no ledger posting. Drafts can mention a fee you decide to charge.

comparison.competitor: Reads customer replies and drafts next steps for review.

comparison.competitor: Xero, QuickBooks Online and Stripe.

whenToChoose.competitor: Choose Paidnice if you invoice in Xero or QuickBooks, have enough invoices that manual chasing eats hours, and want late fees, statements and a payment portal handled for you. Volume-based pricing fits that use.
whenToChoose.docstoc: Choose docstoc if you want a good first draft and the final say. It does not chase on a schedule, apply late fees or post to your ledger.

faq.q: Does Paidnice send emails without my approval?
faq.a: Not before you approve its policies. Its page says nothing runs until you approve them, and fees can be set to wait for your approval. After that, scheduled reminders run on their own.

faq.q: Is docstoc a cheaper Paidnice?
faq.a: On price, yes: $14.99 a month against $69 at the time of writing. The products differ, because docstoc does not automate sending, fees or statements.

faq.q: Can I use both?
faq.a: Yes, but not on the same invoice at the same time. Pause Paidnice reminders for any invoice you chase with a docstoc draft so the client gets one voice.
